Do not uncondense the chowder.

That's a great idea...nothing wrong with adding on to canned soups to make a complete meal. Adding chopped cooked ham or bacon to canned corn chowder is always a favorite. For the OP...Brown rice is always good, but since it takes time to cook I recommend making a big batch and freezing it in ziploc bags: https://www.thekitchn.com/how-to-freeze-cooked-brown-rice-cooking-lessons-from-the-kitchn-177595 then when you are cooking some chicken thighs or other protein on the stove, add the frozen rice in the last 5 minutes of cooking to heat up and absorb the seasonings and juices of the meat (don't need to defrost the rice).

I like a cookbook I got from a thrift store: "Quick and Easy Meals for two" by Louella Shouer (available on the usual book-selling sites)...it's a 50s/60s book aimed at young wives with little knowledge of cooking, teaches basic cooking techniques...from "how to make coffee / steam veggies / roast meat / deep fry / make a salad dressing" etc, and has plenty of simple and reliable recipes. So essentially this recipe but I normally do lamb chops and make as follows:

  1. Heat fry deep fry pan/skillet
  2. Add Italian herb mix and 2 garlic cloves, mix till lightly brown
  3. Lightly melt lots of butter in deep fry pan
  4. Add meat, turning and basting as needed.
  5. 5 minutes before meat is done add asparagus (and broccolini, if room permits) and more butter (does not have to be pre-melted), husband says if in doubt add more butter.

Serve with roasted potatoes cooked with butter and herb mix if very hungry.
